items.stem: A reply from the model contains a request to run a tool, and also a closing sentence that reads like a conclusion. What should the loop do?

options.a: Treat the sentence as the answer and finish, to save a turn
options.b: Carry out what was asked and go on to the next turn
options.c: Ask the model to repeat the reply without the request
options.d: End the run and report that the reply was ambiguous

items.explanation: A reply that holds a tool request is not the end, whatever its text says; the model's stop value marks the end of a turn.

items.stem: A team reads the usage figure on a lead agent's result and reports it as the cost of a whole research run with four helpers. What is wrong?

options.a: Helpers are free of charge when the lead agent pays for the window
options.b: The count covers a single loop, and a separate field exists for the entire tree
options.c: The figure is correct, because a lead agent sums its helpers automatically
options.d: The figure counts only output tokens, so input must be added by hand

items.explanation: The usage figure counts a single loop; the documentation names the field for the whole tree of agents.

items.stem: Two lookups in a plan depend on each other: the second needs the first one's result. How should they be issued?

options.a: In two separate turns, because calls made together carry no promised order
options.b: In one turn, listed in the order in which they are needed by the plan
options.c: In one turn, with a note telling the SDK to run them in sequence
options.d: In parallel, and then repair the second call if it happens to fail

items.explanation: The model decides what to ask for within one turn and the SDK promises no order among calls made together, so a dependency needs two turns.

items.stem: A coordinator located the failing file and the precise message before delegating a fix. What must the helper's prompt contain?

options.a: Only the goal, because the helper will rediscover the rest on its own
options.b: The path, the error text and the decisions already taken
options.c: A pointer to the coordinator's conversation, which the helper can read
options.d: Nothing extra, since subagents inherit what the lead knows

items.explanation: A subagent's context starts fresh, so its brief is the only channel for what the coordinator already found.

items.stem: Two research helpers return largely the same findings. Where should the team look for the cause?

options.a: At the model tier, which is too small to tell the topics apart in a long run
options.b: At the merge step, which should have removed repeated lines before the report in the end
options.c: At the helpers' tool lists, which are probably too long for a narrow task
options.d: At the briefs, which neither split the scope nor said what each part leaves out

items.explanation: Overlap comes from the briefs, since subagents cannot see each other and only the brief divides the work.

items.stem: A question asks for one dated fact that a single search can answer. How large should the team be?

options.a: Three workers, so that the answer is cross-checked every time
options.b: One worker with a few tool calls, since effort should follow the ask
options.c: A coordinator plus one worker per source type, as the default shape at that point
options.d: As many as the budget allows, because more agents never hurt

items.explanation: The documentation's guidance is that simple fact-finding needs just one agent with a few tool calls; the team scales with the ask.

items.stem: A subagent for one narrow job exists, but the model almost never delegates to it. What is the first thing to change?

options.a: Its model, to a larger tier that follows instructions more closely
options.b: Its name, to something longer and more formal in style
options.c: Its system prompt, to say in capitals that it is very important
options.d: Its description, so that it says when the helper should be called

items.explanation: The model reads the description to decide whether to delegate, so the description must state when the agent applies.

items.stem: A coordinator needs a helper's result before it can write the next step, but the work was launched without waiting. What was missing?

options.a: A higher turn limit on the coordinator
options.b: A request for a foreground run
options.c: A hook that blocks until the helper finishes
options.d: A larger context window for the helper

items.explanation: The documented default is a background launch, so a coordinator that needs the result first has to ask for a foreground run.

items.stem: Two helpers cite the same fact from different sources. How should their results come back so that the combining step keeps both sources?

options.a: As one paragraph of prose for each helper, joined together in order
options.b: As a single combined score for each helper's results across the run
options.c: With each claim and its origin in separate fields, joined on the claim
options.d: With the sources dropped, since the claim is what matters to the reader

items.explanation: Content and metadata in separate fields let the merge recognise one claim and keep every source.

items.stem: A refund tool is called before the customer's identity check. What should the gate return?

options.a: An empty success, so the model carries on without a result
options.b: A flagged failure that names the missing step
options.c: A generic error with no detail, to avoid revealing the rules
options.d: Nothing at all, leaving the call unanswered until a timeout

items.explanation: Every call needs an answer, and an error that names the missing step lets the model do it and try again.

items.stem: A team forces the lookup tool on the first request to make sure verification happens before refunds. A refund still follows a failed check on turn five. Why?

options.a: Forced choices expire after a fixed number of seconds
options.b: Refund tools ignore any choice setting by design
options.c: The model disables the setting once it has used the tool
options.d: The choice binds only the call that sets it

items.explanation: A forced tool choice applies to the request that sets it, and nothing carries it to later calls.

items.stem: A hand-off to a person is routed through a verification step, and a fault in that step leaves customers stranded. What is the design flaw?

options.a: The route to a person should be slower, to discourage its use
options.b: The verification step should be removed from every path
options.c: The way out depends on the very safeguard that tripped
options.d: The hand-off should be decided by the model alone

items.explanation: An escape route must not sit behind a prerequisite that may be what failed.

items.stem: A hook should lint only when a command that changes files runs, but it fires on every command. What is the usual fix?

options.a: Match on the file path in the matcher, which is able to read tool inputs
options.b: Run it only in the first turn of each session, then switch it off
options.c: Attach it to the editing tools and test the path inside the callback
options.d: Add a line to the prompt asking the model to avoid every other tool

items.explanation: A matcher sees only the name of the tool, so the path must be read from the input inside the callback.

items.stem: A team wants a payment checked before it is sent. Which placement works?

options.a: A hook that runs ahead of the call and holds it back when needed
options.b: A hook that runs after the tool returns and reports the outcome at that moment
options.c: A hook on the session start, with a reminder of the policy
options.d: A hook on the final answer, which reviews what was done

items.explanation: A post hook runs after the effect, so the money has already moved; the control belongs ahead of the call.

items.stem: A gate hook waits for a person to approve an action and no reply arrives before its deadline. What should happen?

options.a: The operation is withheld and the model is told that no approval came
options.b: The action runs, since silence means that nobody objected to it
options.c: The action runs once and is logged for a later review by a person
options.d: The whole session is closed and returns an error result to the caller

items.explanation: A timed-out gate is the safe case: nothing runs and the model is told.

items.stem: A change touches fourteen files in separate packages. What review shape does the page prefer?

options.a: One review of all fourteen files in a single long prompt
options.b: A review of the three largest files, assuming the rest follow
options.c: A full pass over each document in its own context
options.d: Reviews of the files in sequence, each seeing the previous reports

items.explanation: Each file gets a full review in its own context, and a second pass sees the relations between them.

items.stem: A planning loop proposes the same subtask for the third time. What should it do?

options.a: Raise the turn ceiling so that it can try again
options.b: Halt with a stuck status that names the repeated step
options.c: Drop the subtask quietly and finish the others
options.d: Rephrase the subtask so that it counts as new

items.explanation: A repeated subtask is a lack of progress, and a status says so.

items.stem: Between two review passes the first pass must hand its findings to the second. What should the hand-over contain?

options.a: A name and a short summary for each part, with what it offers and expects
options.b: The complete text of the files that the first pass has read so far
options.c: The number of findings that the first pass made in each part
options.d: Nothing at all, since the second pass will read the same files again

items.explanation: Summaries are the interface between the passes.

items.stem: A developer wants to try a risky refactor from the middle of a saved session without losing the original line of work. What should be done?

options.a: Resume the same id twice at once and edit both
options.b: Resume with the stored id and the fork option
options.c: Start a new session and paste the old transcript
options.d: Edit the stored session file and keep a backup

items.explanation: Fork is an option set together with a resume id; it branches a copy and leaves the original usable.

items.stem: A resumed session gives slow, costly first answers after a weekend. What is the likely cause?

options.a: The saved session has been compressed and must be unpacked
options.b: The prompt cache expired while the work sat idle over two days
options.c: The model was downgraded while the session was idle
options.d: Resuming always repeats every tool call from the start

items.explanation: The prompt cache expires after a long pause, so the next request reads the history once more.

items.stem: After an agent's edits went wrong, a developer wants the files back as they were an hour ago. Which feature does that?

options.a: Resuming the conversation from an earlier message in the transcript
options.b: Forking the session at the point where the hour began
options.c: Checkpointing, which snapshots changes and reverts them
options.d: Clearing the context and starting the work again from the beginning

items.explanation: Only a snapshot of the files can return them to an earlier state; conversation features do not touch the files.

items.stem: Logs show that an agent picks a customer lookup when asked about orders. Both tools have a one-line summary. What does the page rank first?

options.a: Describe the inputs of each one, with sample requests and where it stops
options.b: Add many worked order examples to the system prompt for the model
options.c: Route each request with keyword rules before the model reads it
options.d: Merge the two tools into one that guesses which backend to ask

items.explanation: The cause is thin descriptions, and the first fix is to make each say what it takes and where it stops.

items.stem: An agent calls a tool that finds records, and a broad question returns thousands of them in one reply. What should the tool return?

options.a: The first hundred hits, with no note about the rest of the results
options.b: One page with a cursor, plus a note on how to narrow the query
options.c: Every hit, because the model can ignore whatever it does not need
options.d: A count only, with no hits at all until the agent asks twice

items.explanation: A page with a cursor bounds the result, and the note tells the agent how to go on.

items.stem: After two rounds of rewording, the agent still chooses between two tools at random. What does the page conclude?

options.a: The model is too weak and should be replaced by a larger tier of the family for the team
options.b: The prompt needs a stronger instruction to choose with great care each time
options.c: More worked examples will eventually separate the tools for the model
options.d: The interface needs a redesign, because the texts cannot separate the options

items.explanation: Repeated wrong selection means the tools cannot be told apart from their texts, which is a design fault.

items.stem: A tool fails with only the text 'operation failed'. What should the reply add so that an agent can act?

options.a: A longer stack trace copied from the server and shown to the agent
options.b: An apology that is meant to be shown to the customer in the reply
options.c: The kind of problem, whether a retry helps and what to do next
options.d: A numeric code whose meaning only the developers know by heart

items.explanation: The agent can only choose a recovery if the reply says which one applies.

items.stem: A payment call timed out and nobody knows whether it went through. What should the agent do?

options.a: Repeat the call at once, since a retry is always safe for a payment
options.b: Tell the customer that the payment failed and ask them to try again
options.c: Cancel the whole order to be on the safe side and start it over
options.d: Read the records for the order, then decide if any work remains

items.explanation: A write that may have happened is followed by a read, not by a blind repeat.

items.stem: A search helper times out and its coordinator must choose between a retry and another route. What should the failure carry?

options.a: The kind of fault, the query, partial findings and other paths to try
options.b: Only the word failed, kept short so that the coordinator can read it fast
options.c: The full transcript of the helper's own session, from start to end
options.d: A guess at who is to blame for the delay, with a rough estimate

items.explanation: The coordinator needs the context to choose a recovery.

items.stem: A research helper needs to confirm easy facts, but giving it a full web search causes misuse. What does the page propose?

options.a: A narrow verifier for light checks, with hard cases sent through the hub
options.b: The full version with a warning in its prompt about careful use
options.c: No extra tool, with all checks done by the coordinator itself
options.d: A second full version of it as a backup for the first

items.explanation: A narrow tool serves the frequent case and the coordinator keeps the rare one.

items.stem: A team edits the wording of one tool between runs and finds that saved prompt reads stop. What explains it?

options.a: Saved reads work only for plain text that carries no tool definitions at all in the meantime
options.b: Definitions form the first layer, so a change invalidates every layer after it
options.c: Edits to a tool reset the model's memory of the earlier turns of the chat
options.d: The saved reads expire whenever any file in the working directory is saved

items.explanation: Changing the definitions changes the first layer of the cache, and every layer after it.

items.stem: An irreversible call is within the spending cap. What does the page require?

options.a: Automatic approval, since the spending cap already applies to the call
options.b: A flagged refusal that waits for a person's sign-off on that request
options.c: A second model's opinion given in place of a person's decision
options.d: A warning written to the log after the call has already run

items.explanation: An irreversible call waits for a person even under the cap.

items.stem: A remote server entry sets an Authorization header from ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, and the server sees it empty. What is the likely reason?

options.a: The variable is too long to fit in a header value for that endpoint on that path
options.b: Remote servers refuse every header unless the user types it by hand
options.c: The header is sent only after the first tool call of the session
options.d: Nothing is sent for credential labels of that kind to a far endpoint

items.explanation: Credential names such as this one read as empty toward a remote endpoint.

items.stem: A tool's description is long, with the rule that tells when to prefer it in the last paragraph. What should change?

options.a: Move the whole description into the system prompt and shorten the tool's own text
options.b: Cut it down to the tool's name only, to keep the definition small
options.c: Add an example of a wrong call at the end of the description
options.d: Say when it beats pattern matching and what comes back, point first

items.explanation: The description is what the model chooses by, so it must say when to prefer the tool, with the point first.

items.stem: A team connects one server whose single tool does everything. Why does that make permissions hard?

options.a: Permission rules apply only to the built-in tools of the product
options.b: Servers that offer a single tool cannot be denied by any rule
options.c: Each call of such a server needs a separate approval prompt
options.d: A rule allows or denies one by name, so lone entry leaves nothing to narrow

items.explanation: A permission rule can allow or deny a tool by name, so one tool that does everything leaves nothing to scope.

items.stem: An agent must list every test file that ends in a given suffix. Which built-in does that?

options.a: The content search with a regular expression, run across the tree
options.b: The reader, called on each folder in turn until all are covered
options.c: The shell with a listing command piped into a filter
options.d: The pattern search that matches names, supplied with the product

items.explanation: The job is matching names, which is what a name pattern search is for.

items.stem: A deny rule blocks reading a secrets folder. Can the agent still write a file in that folder?

options.a: No, because a ban on viewing covers the tools that change content there
options.b: Yes, because only views were denied in the settings of the project
options.c: Yes, but after an approval prompt appears for each write
options.d: Through the shell, which sits outside such rules

items.explanation: A read denial covers the tools that change content at the same path.

items.stem: A deny rule on one text-search tool does not stop a search on a Linux machine. Why?

options.a: Deny rules apply to tools that have already been loaded in the session
options.b: Linux ignores permission rules for searches in the working directory
options.c: The default set lacks a dedicated grep utility there, and a shell does the work
options.d: Such rules work when the tool name is written in uppercase

items.explanation: On macOS, Linux and WSL the default set has no Grep, so only a shell entry sees those lookups.

items.stem: A developer wants personal preferences for one project that never reach teammates. Where do they belong?

options.a: The root instruction file, which every clone shares
options.b: A rule file with no path list in the shared folder
options.c: The home-folder file that applies to every project
options.d: A git-ignored local file beside the root instruction file

items.explanation: The local file is personal to one project and is kept out of version control.

items.stem: A team restricts a testing guideline to test files by path, yet it loads on every file. Its frontmatter has a stray tab. What happened?

options.a: The header block did not parse, so the entry applies everywhere
options.b: A tab makes a rule apply to the whole directory tree under the project
options.c: The rule loads once for each tab character that it contains
options.d: Errors in the frontmatter switch the rule off completely

items.explanation: When the frontmatter does not parse, the rule is treated as unscoped.

items.stem: A project holds an AGENTS.md and a git-ignored personal file named for CLAUDE.md. Is the AGENTS.md read?

options.a: Yes, because AGENTS.md is read in every project, whatever else exists there
options.b: No, because the fallback runs only when no memory document exists, and that memo is one
options.c: Yes, but only when the local file happens to be completely empty
options.d: No, because AGENTS.md is read only in headless runs and never in a session

items.explanation: AGENTS.md is read only when no CLAUDE.md file exists in the working directory or above, and the local file counts.

items.stem: A command file and a skill carry the same name. Which does Claude use?

options.a: The older format, since it was created first and is therefore the original
options.b: Both of them, one after the other in alphabetical order of path
options.c: The newer format, which takes precedence over the older one
options.d: Neither, since a name that is shared makes the lookup ambiguous

items.explanation: The product merged the two formats and gives the skill precedence over a command file of the same name.

items.stem: A skill lists an item in its allowed-tools field. What does that field do?

options.a: It removes the other tools from the session while the skill runs
options.b: It makes that item available in later sessions of the project
options.c: It pre-approves the named entry, with nothing else restricted by it
options.d: It forbids the model from using a further skill during the run

items.explanation: The field pre-approves and restricts nothing.

items.stem: A forked skill's body is only a list of style guidelines, and it returns nothing useful. Why?

options.a: The text is the helper's prompt, and formatting advice alone gives it no task
options.b: Forked skills are unable to read their own file when they start
options.c: Guidelines are ignored by a helper unless they are numbered
options.d: The helper needs a larger model tier than the main session

items.explanation: A forked skill's body is its prompt, and guidelines without a task give the helper nothing to do.

items.stem: A request touches many files and has two plausible designs. How should the work start?

options.a: With edits in the most likely files, followed by a review of the diff
options.b: With a test run first, to see which checks fail at the start
options.c: With one sentence in the prompt asking the model to be careful
options.d: In plan mode, researching first and settling the approach before any edit

items.explanation: Many files and several valid approaches both argue for planning first.

items.stem: An instruction is read differently each time it runs. Which fix does the page prefer?

options.a: A longer description of the intent, written out in plain prose
options.b: A stronger word such as always or never in front of the rule
options.c: Two or three exact inputs paired with the required outputs
options.d: A request to the model to explain how it reads the rule

items.explanation: Exact examples remove the ambiguity that causes inconsistent reading.

items.stem: A developer has corrected the same mistake three times and the session keeps drifting. What is the documented step?

options.a: Make a fourth correction in the same session, with firmer wording
options.b: Switch to a larger model and keep the same long session going
options.c: Wait for the context to compact itself and then try once more
options.d: Clear the context and write a better first prompt, carrying what was learned

items.explanation: After more than two failed corrections the documented fix is to clear the context and write a better first prompt.

items.stem: A job needs a review in a form that a script can read. Which options give a validated object?

options.a: The text format with a request for a table
options.b: The JSON output setting together with a JSON schema
options.c: The streaming format with a final marker line
options.d: The default format and a regular expression

items.explanation: The schema makes the answer a validated object in the structured output field.

items.stem: A job that reviews code posts the same findings again after each push. What is the fix?

options.a: Raise the sampling temperature, so that each run gives more variety
options.b: Add earlier reports to the prompt and ask for new issues only
options.c: Resume the earlier run inside the new job, to carry its memory
options.d: Ask for fewer findings in the criteria of the review prompt

items.explanation: A run has no memory of the last one, so what was reported must be in the prompt.

items.stem: A review job run in the minimal startup mode ignores the project's review rules. Why, and what is the fix?

options.a: Bare mode switches off all rules, so none can be added to it at all
options.b: The rules load only on a scheduled run and never on a push
options.c: The rules must first move into the settings file of the project
options.d: Skipping the memory file is the cause, so a prompt-file option supplies them

items.explanation: Bare mode skips CLAUDE.md, so the criteria must be passed in by hand.

items.stem: A review prompt says 'be conservative', and developers still see noisy findings. What changes the output?

options.a: Name the patterns to flag and the ones to leave alone
options.b: Add the word very in front of conservative in the sentence
options.c: Lower the limit on the number of findings that each run can report
options.d: Run the review twice and keep only the findings that overlap

items.explanation: Naming the patterns to report and to skip is what changes the output.

items.stem: An unattended run lacks a required field that has no default. What should it do?

options.a: Ask the developer a question and wait for an answer to come back
options.b: Stop with a plain failure that names what is absent
options.c: Fill the field with a likely value and go on with the run
options.d: Skip the task and report that the run was a success

items.explanation: An unattended run cannot ask, and a required field with no default cannot be assumed.

items.stem: Reviewers dismiss most findings from one category. What does the page suggest?

options.a: Fix the criteria for that one group and keep the others enabled
options.b: Disable all groups until the trust of the reviewers has returned
options.c: Raise the severity floor for the findings of each group at once
options.d: Remove the reviewers' ability to dismiss a finding

items.explanation: The recorded pattern shows where the dismissals come from, so only that part is adjusted.

items.stem: An invoice schema makes every field required, and some vendor names in the output do not occur in the documents. What is the first fix?

options.a: Add a line to the prompt asking the model not to invent anything
options.b: Allow a null where the source does not give a value
options.c: Raise the sampling temperature of the model for that one field
options.d: Add a second model whose job is to rewrite the vendor names

items.explanation: A field that may be missing from the source should be nullable so that the model is not pushed to fabricate.

items.stem: Line items add up to 90 and the total field reads 100, yet the record passes its strict schema. What follows?

options.a: Shape is promised and meaning is not, so code must compare the sums
options.b: The schema is wrong and must be made stricter with more fields
options.c: The model should be asked to add up the items more carefully
options.d: The record is valid, since the schema accepted it as it stands

items.explanation: Strict schemas do not prevent semantic errors, and a sum is one.

items.stem: A record's total disagrees with its line items and a retry gives the same difference. What does the page treat the case as?

options.a: A conflict to route to a person, with the discrepancy noted
options.b: A model fault that a larger model would fix on the next attempt
options.c: A schema fault that a new field in the schema would remove
options.d: A transient error that a retry will clear if it is repeated

items.explanation: A flagged conflict is information about a bad source, and a second look finds the same difference.

items.stem: A merge verdict holds up a developer, and a weekly dependency scan has no deadline. Which one goes through the batch interface?

options.a: Both of them, with polling to learn when the verdict is ready
options.b: The verdict only, since a blocking check is the more valuable
options.c: Neither of them, since batches cannot carry long text inputs
options.d: The one on the calendar, leaving the blocking check on the immediate path

items.explanation: A merge verdict is a blocking check that cannot wait for a window without a latency guarantee.

items.stem: A second pass in the same session approves a change that the first pass wrote. Why is that weak?

options.a: Two passes inside one session always return exactly the same text of the work
options.b: The second pass quietly uses a cheaper tier by default
options.c: A session limits itself to a single review of any change
options.d: The reasoning behind the edit is still present and biases the check

items.explanation: The reasoning that justified the code is still in the context, so a fresh instance sees the change without it.

items.stem: A prompt is ready for a million documents. What does the page do first?

options.a: Submit the whole corpus in one batch at once, to save cost on the run
options.b: Run the first ten documents only and assume the rest will behave
options.c: A varied sample run synchronously, with long and incomplete inputs among it
options.d: Ask the model to estimate its own accuracy and trust the figure

items.explanation: A prompt is proven on a sample that includes the awkward documents, run synchronously so the answer comes at once.

items.stem: Amounts and dates drift in a long support chat after the history is condensed. What is the fix?

options.a: Condense the history less often, so that fewer rounds can occur
options.b: Ask the model to repeat the figures at the end of each reply
options.c: Switch to a model with a longer window and keep the same text
options.d: A structured block of exact values, sent with every request

items.explanation: The exact values leave the text that gets condensed, so no round of condensing can round them off.

items.stem: Two records give different delivery dates, and the older one arrives later. Which is current?

options.a: The one carrying the newer stamp
options.b: The one that arrived last in the stream of incoming records
options.c: The one that the customer happened to mention in the chat
options.d: Neither of them, until a person has decided which to keep

items.explanation: The date decides, so the late older value goes to the history and the current value is untouched.

items.stem: An agent serves several customers and must never show one the records of another. Where is the control?

options.a: In the system prompt, with an instruction to stay within the customer's data
options.b: In the model itself, which has been trained to separate customers
options.c: In code that filters by the authenticated key before the context is built
options.d: In the reply, which is checked afterwards for names of other people

items.explanation: The identity comes from the session the application holds, and the exclusion happens in code before the model sees anything.

items.stem: A customer writes 'let me talk to a person'. What does the agent do first?

options.a: Look up the account and try to solve the problem
options.b: Hand over at once, without investigating the account
options.c: Ask why the customer wants a person
options.d: Offer a discount to keep the conversation

items.explanation: An explicit request for a person is honoured at once, with no investigation first.

items.stem: A name matches three customers. Which handling does the page prefer?

options.a: The account with the most recent activity, on the assumption that it is meant
options.b: The first match in the list, confirmed with the caller at the end
options.c: An identifier that tells them apart, such as the email held on file
options.d: A merged view of all three accounts shown in one reply

items.explanation: The agent asks for something that tells the candidates apart and leaves the choice to the caller's answer.

items.stem: Two tries at a refund have made no progress. What should happen?

options.a: It tries a third time with a rephrased prompt and a gentler tone
options.b: It stops at the cap and hands over a short summary of what was tried
options.c: It closes the case as resolved and sends a satisfaction survey
options.d: It asks the customer to call back later when the system is quiet

items.explanation: Two attempts without progress hit the third trigger, and the hand-off carries what was tried.

items.stem: A search helper hits a transient timeout. Who should retry?

options.a: The coordinator, which repeats every failed call on the helper's behalf
options.b: The user, who is given a notice of failure and asked to retry
options.c: The worker itself, passing up only what it cannot resolve
options.d: Nobody, since a timeout in a search is always final and fatal

items.explanation: The subagent holds the query and the work done, so it retries what is transient and reports only what survives.

items.stem: A helper returns an empty list after a timeout, and the coordinator takes it as 'no results'. What is wrong?

options.a: Empty lists should be reported to the user as failures of the run
options.b: The coordinator should simply wait longer for the list to fill
options.c: Timeouts should be hidden from the coordinator to keep it simple
options.d: A failure and a reply with no matches differ in kind and in handling

items.explanation: A failure and a valid empty result are different values with different handling.

items.stem: One of four research topics is shut to the agent. What should the run do?

options.a: Stop at once and discard everything that has been gathered so far
options.b: Carry on with the other three and log the closed area as a gap to reopen
options.c: Fill the topic from the model's memory and mark it as covered
options.d: Retry the closed topic over and over until it finally opens

items.explanation: Terminating on one failure wastes the other work, and a refusal is recorded as a gap with the way to get access.

items.stem: An exploration of a large codebase fills the context with files of little value. Which technique keeps the lead's context small?

options.a: Open the whole tree in one long conversation and trim the context later
options.b: Keep all of the files and rely on automatic summarising to cope
options.c: Ask the model to forget the old files once it has read them
options.d: Read-only helpers answer each question and return only a summary

items.explanation: Each narrow question goes to a read-only subagent, and the coordinator receives only a summary.

items.stem: After a crash, some helpers have stored progress and some do not. What is the recovery?

options.a: Restart every helper from nothing, whether or not it kept anything
options.b: Continue all helpers from their last reported status line
options.c: Continue those that kept something, and begin the others afresh
options.d: Ask the helpers which of them ought to be restarted

items.explanation: The agents with files continue from them and the others start over, since the file outranks the status.

items.stem: Which kind of helper can be resumed later with its own history?

options.a: The built-in exploring subagent that ships with the product
options.b: Any helper that was launched in the background of a session
options.c: A custom subagent, not the built-in one
options.d: Only a helper that has already finished its job successfully

items.explanation: A custom subagent can be resumed with its history, and the built-in one cannot.

items.stem: An extraction pipeline reports 96 percent overall, and the team proposes dropping review. What should come first?

options.a: A larger sample drawn from the easy documents of the stream
options.b: A second run of the same pipeline with a stronger model
options.c: A breakdown by document kind and by field
options.d: A vote among the reviewers about whether the figure feels right

items.explanation: The overall figure is an average dominated by the large easy segment, so each kind and field is measured on its own.

items.stem: A reviewing team can read only half of the flagged items today. Which half comes first?

options.a: The oldest items, in order of arrival
options.b: The most certain items, to clear them quickly
options.c: Conflicts and the least certain entries
options.d: A random half, for fairness

items.explanation: Conflicts and the lowest confidence are read first and the overflow waits, visibly, in a backlog.

items.stem: An agent's refund over a limit may go ahead when its confidence is high. What does the page say?

options.a: Yes, since high confidence is the very purpose of the score
options.b: Yes, whenever the score is above ninety percent on the record
options.c: No, since an action on the irreversible list always needs a person
options.d: No, unless the customer has asked for the refund twice

items.explanation: An action on the irreversible list always needs a person, whatever the confidence.

items.stem: Two sources give different figures for the same measure. How should the report present them?

options.a: The higher value, shown as the safer estimate for the reader
options.b: Both values, each with its origin and a note that they disagree
options.c: The average of the two values, rounded to a convenient figure
options.d: The value from the more recent source only, with no mention of the other

items.explanation: The guide's answer is annotating conflicts with source attribution rather than arbitrarily selecting one value.

items.stem: A summarising stage must not lose where each claim came from. What does the page require?

options.a: A list of the sources placed at the end of the final report
options.b: A note in the prompt asking the model to remember its sources
options.c: Each statement paired with its origin as structured data at every exchange
options.d: One source named for the whole run, in the title of the report

items.explanation: A compression step keeps the origin next to the text it produces, so the pairing survives every step.

items.stem: A subagent cannot trace a statement to any source. What should it return?

options.a: Report it as unattributed in a separate place, or leave it out
options.b: Return it with a source guessed from the topic of the question
options.c: Return it as established, since it sounds right to the model
options.d: Return it with a high confidence figure attached to the claim

items.explanation: A statement with no source is reported separately as unsourced, or left out.

items.stem: A support agent moves money too early because tools can be called in any sequence. What is the first fix?

options.a: Add a much stronger sentence about the order to the prompt
options.b: Rename the tools so that the right order is obvious from them
options.c: Review the transcripts once a week and correct the mistakes
options.d: Enforce the order of calls in the dispatcher, in code

items.explanation: Money that moved wrongly cannot be recalled, so the cause is fixed first, in code.

items.stem: A team celebrates a lower escalation rate. Which check shows whether it is a real success?

options.a: If cases settled alone although a person was needed did not rise
options.b: Whether the average session has become shorter over the month
options.c: Whether the model's own stated confidence has risen over time
options.d: Whether customers now write fewer messages in each conversation over the month

items.explanation: A lower escalation rate is a success only if no case that needed a person was settled alone.

items.stem: State from one support ticket reaches the next one. What is the fix?

options.a: Clear the conversation every ten minutes during a long working day
options.b: Ask the model to forget the earlier ticket when the next begins
options.c: Run the tickets in strict alphabetical order of customer name
options.d: Create a fresh instance per case so that nothing outlives it

items.explanation: A state that belongs to one case cannot reach another.

items.stem: Where should a team's review command live so that a new teammate gets it with the first checkout?

options.a: The home folder of its author, where personal commands usually sit
options.b: A list of commands written inside the root memory file
options.c: A settings array of commands that Claude Code reads at start
options.d: The project's own configuration directory, committed with the sources

items.explanation: A command file in the project's own folder is committed and reaches every clone.

items.stem: A rule's paths entry names a directory, src/api, and the rule never loads. What is wrong?

options.a: A bare label is not a glob, so it matches no file
options.b: The folder is too deep in the tree for any rule to reach it
options.c: Rules load only for files that sit at the root of the project
options.d: The entry needs a trailing space after the name to be read

items.explanation: A bare folder name is not a glob; write a folder as src/api/** so that it matches files beneath.

items.stem: Which task is best started by thinking through the design first and which by a single edit?

options.a: Both of them in plan mode, as a rule of the team
options.b: Both of them directly, with a test run after each change
options.c: Restructuring a monolith in plan mode, and a typo fix done directly
options.d: The typo fix in plan mode, and the monolith done directly

items.explanation: Small clear work is direct and open design is plan.

items.stem: A research report lacks a whole topic, yet every helper did its job. What does the team check first?

options.a: The tool list of each of the helpers that took part in the run
options.b: The prompt of the report writer that produced the final text
options.c: The coordinator's plan, compared with the scopes of the question
options.d: The index of the search provider that the helpers queried

items.explanation: The subagents did what they were assigned, so the plan is what to check.

items.stem: A run covered three of four scopes and one source pair disagrees. What does the report carry?

options.a: A complete status, since three scopes out of four is a majority
options.b: A partial status, listing the missing area and the conflict
options.c: A failed status, with no report at all for the reader
options.d: A complete status, with the disagreement quietly removed

items.explanation: A missing scope makes the run partial, and a conflict is reported next to it.

items.stem: A search for one scope times out, and an alternative query exists. What should the run do?

options.a: Retry the first query again and again until it finally succeeds
options.b: Retry once through the substitute, then give the area up
options.c: Skip the scope without any mention in the final report
options.d: Report the scope as covered, since an alternative query was tried

items.explanation: One retry through the alternative, then an honest gap.

items.stem: An agent should write only inside a generated folder. Which rule does that?

options.a: An edit permission limited to that directory, instead of one for the whole tool
options.b: An allow rule for the Write tool with no path attached to it at all
options.c: A line in the prompt that names the directory and asks for great care
options.d: A deny rule for every other directory, written out one by one

items.explanation: An allow rule that covers the whole tool is the fault; a path keeps the rule to one folder.

items.stem: A server definition file holds a token header with a literal value. What does the audit say?

options.a: A secret sits in a committed document, so a variable reference should replace it
options.b: Nothing is wrong, since tokens in such a file are public by design
options.c: The header is fine as long as the repository itself is private
options.d: The header only needs to be renamed so that it looks less like a secret

items.explanation: A header whose name says token and whose value has no variable reference is a secret in the file.

items.stem: A team note about server setup must list what?

options.a: Only the variables that hold secrets, since the rest are harmless
options.b: Only the variables that already carry a default value
options.c: The names of the tools that the servers offer to the agent
options.d: Every variable that the backends need in order to start up

items.explanation: Every variable that appears in the project's server file has to appear in the note.

items.stem: A build job launches Claude Code with a prompt and stalls until the runner times it out. Which change fixes the step?

options.a: Add the print flag so that the run answers and exits
options.b: Redirect standard input from an empty file at the start of the step
options.c: Set an environment variable that tells the tool it runs headless
options.d: Add a flag on the command line that turns the run into a batch

items.explanation: The print flag is the documented way to run without a person; the other options do not exist or are workarounds.

items.stem: A nightly digest and a merge gate both call the model. Which one fits the batch interface?

options.a: The gate, since a merge check is the more important of the two
options.b: Both of them, with a fallback to real time if the batch is slow
options.c: Neither of them, since the results of a batch arrive out of order
options.d: The summary job, since nobody waits for it

items.explanation: Nobody waits for the digest and a developer waits for the gate.

items.stem: A review of a large change is split into passes. Which split does the page use?

options.a: One single pass over the whole change in a long prompt
options.b: A separate pass for each persona of reviewer on the team
options.c: A separate pass for each severity level of finding
options.d: A pass for each file, then an integration pass over the findings

items.explanation: A pass for each file, then the integration pass.

items.stem: A document does not contain a required value. What does the pipeline do after the first attempt?

options.a: Retries with a higher temperature until a value appears
options.b: Fills the value in from similar documents that were seen before
options.c: Sends it to a person, since no retry gives what the page omits
options.d: Marks the record valid with the field left empty

items.explanation: A missing value is routed, not retried.

items.stem: A kind of document has exactly the minimum count and accuracy exactly at the target. Is it automated?

options.a: No, because accuracy must exceed the target and not merely equal it
options.b: No, because fifty documents is never enough for any kind
options.c: Only after another month of data has been collected for the kind
options.d: Yes, if that tally meets the floor, since both tests are inclusive

items.explanation: Both comparisons are inclusive, so reaching the evidence is enough.

items.stem: Accuracy on validated records is higher than accuracy on all records by exactly the policy margin. Is the figure overstated?

options.a: No, since a difference that only reaches the limit does not exceed it
options.b: Yes, since any positive difference at all makes the figure overstated
options.c: Yes, since the figure is rounded before the two are compared
options.d: Only if the target is missed as well as the gap being reached

items.explanation: A difference that reaches the gap is not overstated.

items.stem: A message from a user shows signs of risk. What happens first?

options.a: The assistant answers the message first and then offers some help
options.b: The assistant asks a few clarifying questions about the situation
options.c: It goes to a safety hand-off before any other handling
options.d: The assistant logs the message for the weekly review by the team

items.explanation: Risk is checked first.

items.stem: Three of twenty sampled conversations repeated a question, and the policy accepts up to ten percent. What does the review conclude?

options.a: The batch fails, since the share is above the ceiling
options.b: The batch passes, since three is close enough to two in a small run
options.c: The batch passes, since only a repeat of a whole conversation would count
options.d: The review waits for a fourth sample before it concludes anything

items.explanation: Three of twenty is fifteen percent, which is above ten, and a limit is met only at the limit or below.

items.stem: A recalled plan is ten months old and the policy limit is thirty days, yet the assistant states its renewal terms as current. What went wrong?

options.a: Stated as current, since a saved plan is the best evidence there is
options.b: Checked with the person first, and not asserted as true today
options.c: Dropped from the store silently, as nothing so old can be right
options.d: Stated with a warning added at the end of the reply

items.explanation: An old fact is verified before it is used, so the plan should have been confirmed with the person first.

items.stem: Generated tool code fetches a page that its proposal never mentioned. What is the decision?

options.a: Approval, with a note added for the reviewer to read later in the week
options.b: A refusal, because behaviour beyond what was announced is not approved
options.c: Revision, with a request to add the network effect to the proposal
options.d: Approval behind a gate, since the network needs a person to look

items.explanation: An undeclared effect cannot be approved on its behalf.

items.stem: An approved tool is edited by the agent. What must happen before it runs next?

options.a: Nothing needs to happen, since the first approval still stands
options.b: The agent states in the log that the change is only a small one
options.c: It goes through the gate as a new proposal
options.d: A log entry is written afterwards to record what was changed

items.explanation: A changed tool is a new proposal, since the person approved what they read.

items.stem: Where should the audit of tool decisions and runs be kept?

options.a: Where the agent has no write access, written by the gate and the runner
options.b: In a file that the agent maintains for its own convenience
options.c: In the agent's own memory, which it can consult at any time
options.d: In the output of the tool itself, one line for every call

items.explanation: A log that the agent can edit is not an audit.
